ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners against the New Zealand Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the UK HM Treasury Sanctions List. Additionally, Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be identified using a risk-based approach, with enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on an ongoing basis, and upon any trigger event. Results must be documented and retained for at least five years. Any positive match requires immediate escalation to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and suspension of the transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in English or Maori, or a combination thereof. Transliteration is permitted provided it is phonetically accurate and does not mislead. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a legal element (e.g., 'Limited' or 'Ltd'), (2) a distinctive element unique to the company, (3) a descriptive element indicating the business activity, and (4) optional additional words. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), as amended, principally ss 12–16 (incorporation and capacity), ss 20–28 (company names), ss 33–34 (registered office and address for service), Part 5 (share capital and allotment), ss 128–137 (directors' duties) and ss 189–191 (board resolutions and proceedings)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Business Registries and Services, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993, lodged electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand imposes no minimum paid-up share capital or escrow/blocked capital account requirement. Shares may be issued fully paid, partly paid, or nil paid on the terms determined by the directors; the application must state the number of shares, classes, consideration, and the amount paid or unpaid for each share, all in accordance with Part 5 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LTD. AT A MEETING of the Board of Directors (the Board) of the Company, duly convened and held at [place], New Zealand, on [date] at [time] in person and by electronic communication, a quorum of directors being present, and notice having been given as required by the Company constitution and section 189 of the Companies Act 1993, the Chairperson declared that the following resolutions were unanimously adopted by the directors: (1) SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: The subscription for, allotment and issue of [number] ordinary shares in the capital of the Company to the subscribers named in the register of allotment at a subscription price of NZD [amount] per share, be and is hereby approved, ratified, and confirmed. The Board acknowledged that the subscription consideration has been or will be lawfully received by the Company and that such shares are validly issued, fully paid or to be paid, as applicable. The Company Secretary is directed to record the allotment in the share register, issue any share certificates, and deliver any returns required by the Companies Act 1993. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS FOR SERVICE: The registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [physical address], New Zealand, and the address for service be and is hereby fixed at [address]. The Company Secretary is authorized and directed to file all prescribed notices with the Registrar under sections 33 and 34 of the Companies Act 1993 within the statutory period and to update the Companies Register upon any change. (3) BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Company's principal banker be and is hereby designated as [bank and branch], and [name A], [name B], and [name C] be and are hereby appointed as authorized signatories on all accounts, including wire transfer and internet banking facilities. The bank mandate shall require [any one/two] signature(s) as set out in the bank account opening documents, and such signatories are authorized to give indemnities, execute loan documents, and handle all banking formalities until the bank receives a certified board resolution revoking their authority. (4) STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [name A] be and is hereby appointed as Managing Director, [name B] as Finance Director, and [name C] as Company Secretary, each with all authorities granted by the constitution and applicable law, including authority to open accounts, hire staff, execute client contracts, engage legal and tax advisors, and complete all registration and regulatory filings on behalf of the Company. (5) RATIFICATION AND GENERAL AUTHORITY: All acts, documents, contracts, applications, or payments made before the date of this resolution in connection with the formation, organization, or operation of the Company, including the incorporation application, be and are hereby ratified, confirmed, adopted, and approved in all respects, and any one director or the Company Secretary is authorized to sign, execute, deliver, or lodge any certificate, instrument, deed, resolution, or notice required to give effect to these resolutions. This resolution was recorded as a full and true record of the proceedings and is effective immediately upon its passage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Availability and Eligibility Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Companies Register (business services operated by MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before submitting the incorporation application, counsel must search the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm the proposed company name is distinguishable from existing registered names and is not prohibited, offensive, or likely to mislead under the Companies Act 1993. Verify that at least one director will satisfy the statutory residence requirement (ordinarily resident in New Zealand or Australia and not disqualified), confirm the registered office address will be a physical New Zealand address, and ensure the proposed shareholders and directors are not disqualified or subject to unresolved AML/CFT adverse findings. If the name is desirable but pending, request a name reservation for up to 20 working days before completing the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and at least two alternative names
Certified passport/photo identification and proof of residential address for every proposed director and shareholder
AML/KYC questionnaire and source-of-funds evidence for beneficial owners
Signed consent to act for each proposed director and shareholder
Name reservation receipt, if a name reservation was made
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the proposed name as unavailable, prohibited, or misleading, submit a new name through the Companies Register or apply for a name variation; the pre-incorporation screening process does not affect the corporate shell because no incorporation application has yet been filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Application and Constitutional Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office via the Companies Register (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and lodge the electronic Application for Registration of a Company under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993. Enter the entity's legal name, proposed incorporation date, registered office address, address for service, share structure, initial shareholders, and full particulars of every director. Attach a copy of the company constitution, or explicitly elect to adopt the default model constitution contained in the Companies Act 1993. Collect and upload signed consents from directors and shareholders, confirm the registered office owner has authorised use of the premises, pay the applicable state filing fee, and submit the application. Upon successful processing, the Companies Office will issue a certificate of incorporation and allocate a company number and New Zealand Business Number.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of a Company
Company constitution, if adopted, or statutory election for default constitution
Consent and authority from the owner of the proposed registered office premises
Signed consent to become a director for each proposed director
Signed share subscription consent for each initial shareholder
Proof of directorship/residence where any director is a non-individual officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application, correct the flagged particulars and respond within the statutory query window; if registration is suspended or refused, obtain written reasons, amend the application, and resubmit; judicial review under the Companies Act 1993 is available if there are grounds for review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NZBN Activation and Inland Revenue Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) system and Inland Revenue Department (IRD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the Companies Office automatically issues an NZBN. Counsel must complete Inland Revenue entity registration through the secured myIR portal to obtain a corporate IRD number and to register for applicable taxes, including corporate income tax, GST, PAYE, and non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends or interest. The registration must identify the company's financial year-end, business type code (ISIC 7110), expected turnover, and tax residency position of all shareholders. For non-resident shareholders, the controller should preserve all relevant double-taxation-agreement declarations so that any withholding tax can be correctly applied. The IRD registration should be completed before the company issues invoices to clients.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and Companies Register extract
NZBN certificate issued by the Companies Office
Completed IRD entity registration application (myIR online equivalent)
Directors' and shareholders' tax residency declarations
Details of expected business income and payment rails
Authorised officer's contact details and New Zealand address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD delays or rejects the registration, respond to the verification/query through myIR and provide certified identity documents and source documents; if late-filing penalties arise, apply for remission on the ground of reasonable excuse and obtain written confirmation of the effective registration date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Corporate Governance Adoption, and Banking Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors and company secretary/registered agent of the Company (private corporate act; no government license)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, or pass a unanimous written resolution, to approve the pro-forma first board resolution. Adopt the constitution, issue share certificates, approve the allotment of shares, appoint the managing director, finance director, and company secretary, establish the registered office and address for service, and authorise bank account opening. The board must maintain minutes of proceedings, the share register, director register, and statutory records at the registered office. If the company uses an offshore/trust structure, execute properly documented outsourced registered-office and secretarial service agreements. The banking mandate must list beneficial owners under AML/CFT rules and specify wire transfer approval thresholds and Wise/Wire_Transfer utilisation protocols.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting or unanimous written resolution
Share allotment and subscription records
Share certificates or book-entry evidence
Apostilled/notarised corporate good-standing extract, if required by the bank
Bank account opening and AML/CFT beneficial ownership declarations
Registered office service provider agreement and company secretary engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank rejects the corporate banking mandate or requests enhanced due diligence, reissue the board resolution in the bank's prescribed form, provide certified passport copies and a current Companies Register extract, and resubmit; if a director has resigned before the meeting, file the change with the Companies Office before executing the mandate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Compliance Filings, Annual Return, and Calendar Management
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete all post-incorporation notices, including the first annual return and any corrections to the registered office, address for service, director, or shareholder details. Ensure the Companies Register mirrors the actual governance documents and that any constitution amendment is uploaded. For this ISIC 7110 CAD/BIM business, maintain a thin-file accounting and compliance record consistent with the company's low-risk AML profile, retain all client contracts, banking records, and board minutes, and set calendar reminders for annual return filing, IRD return filing, and GST filing deadlines. Confirm that no industrial or physical licensing requirement attaches to the digital engineering services scope. If a physical office is later leased, arrange for Building Warrant of Fitness and health and safety compliance separately.
required_dossiers: Companies Register company extract and NZBN confirmation
Annual return confirmation and scheduled filing calendar
All board resolutions, registers, and share records
IRD online account summary and tax registration confirmations
AML/CFT compliance program and banking periodic-review documents
Insurance policies and professional-indemnity coverage if required by client contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues an annual-return or strike-off notice, file the overdue return immediately and apply for reinstatement if the company has been removed; for any incomplete IRD filing, use the voluntary disclosure procedure to correct the position and minimise penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the registered activity (ISIC 7110, engineering design, CAD drafting, BIM consulting) is a pure digital and consulting service with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or industrial process in New Zealand. For any future office lease, general workplace safety oversight is with WorkSafe New Zealand (MBIE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license, factory permit, manufacturing certificate, or physical-trade license is required for ISIC 7110 CAD/BIM services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no physical operation triggers the environmental consenting jurisdiction of the Environmental Protection Authority under the Resource Management Act 1991; no EPA approval is required for engineering CAD/BIM service delivery.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable - no prescribed activity and no resource consent classification; therefore no Full EIA report, environmental registration, or discharge consent is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial point-source discharge, zero VOC, zero wastewater, and zero hazardous-waste generation arising from the digital service activity. Any administrative e-waste from IT equipment must be lawfully disposed of in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial or civil-defense license. If the company leases a commercial office, the premises must hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004, comply with Fire and Emergency New Zealand evacuation and means-of-escape requirements, and meet the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 worker-protection duties; these are general commercial lease obligations rather than entity-level operating licenses.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Te Tari Taake; online electronic portal myIR at www.ird.govt.nz. Physical export clearance is administered by New Zealand Customs Service (Ngā Ratonga Aroteke) under the Customs and Excise Act 2018.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Determine whether the entity is carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand or is otherwise required to hold an IRD number under the Tax Administration Act 1994. 2. For a New Zealand incorporated limited company, apply to the Companies Office via the New Zealand Companies Office / New Zealand Business Number process and simultaneously apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number. 3. For a foreign non-resident entity, first register as an overseas company with the Companies Office if required, then apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number through the Commissioner-prescribed application available in myIR or in paper form. 4. Complete the GST registration application in myIR or using the prescribed paper application, stating expected annual taxable supplies; compulsory registration arises when total taxable supplies in any 12-month period exceed or are expected to exceed NZD 60,000. 5. Upon approval, Inland Revenue issues a single IRD number that also serves as the GST number and income tax account identifier; maintain a New Zealand postal address or appoint a New Zealand tax agent for correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A New Zealand resident limited company incorporated in New Zealand is taxed at the entity level on worldwide income under the Income Tax Act 2007; the standard corporate income tax rate is 28% from the 2020/21 income year, with no sub-national income tax layers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None in the US check-the-box sense; New Zealand has no optional pass-through check-the-box regime. The Income Tax Act 2007 permits a closely held New Zealand resident company to elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status under subpart HB, which attributes profits to qualifying shareholders and exempts the company-level tax, provided all LTC eligibility requirements are satisfied. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 apply to cross-border structures; no other generic hybrid election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (total taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; non-resident suppliers of remote or digital services to New Zealand consumers are also required to register above this threshold; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based invoice validation mandate from Inland Revenue. GST-registered suppliers must issue valid tax invoices for supplies of NZD 50 or more including GST and must retain records for at least seven years. E-invoicing, including PEPPOL-based e-invoicing, is permitted voluntarily. Physical import and export declarations are lodged with New Zealand Customs Service through the Trade Single Window under the Customs and Excise Act 2018; Inland Revenue operates a risk-based post-return audit model.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under sections 11 and 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985: (1) goods are zero-rated when the supplier exports the goods and the goods are exported within 28 days of the time of supply; (2) services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, which includes offshore civil infrastructure CAD/BIM and structural drafting services, provided the supply is not directly connected with land or tangible goods in New Zealand and is not received by a person in New Zealand for use in New Zealand; (3) the supplier must hold contemporaneous documentary evidence of export or non-resident status and report the supply in the GST return as zero-rated with GST at 0%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged with New Zealand Customs Service through the Trade Single Window under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 (required for tangible export goods; not applicable to a pure digital CAD/BIM service export).
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement of goods, where physical goods are included in the export transaction.

Commercial invoice and contract or statement of work identifying the non-resident customer, the nature of the CAD/BIM services, the consideration, and a statement that the supply is zero-rated for GST.

Bank-issued inward foreign currency receipt evidence such as a SWIFT MT103 or MT202 credit confirmation, or an equivalent bank certificate similar to an Inward Remittance Certificate, showing the export proceeds were credited to the New Zealand exporter's bank account.

Delivery and performance records, including client acceptance emails, cloud platform delivery logs, time logs, or structured data handover records, demonstrating that the services were performed and delivered to the non-resident while the recipient was outside New Zealand.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may retrospectively claw back the 0% GST rate and assess output GST at 15% from the date of supply if the export zero-rating is unsupported by documents or if goods or services are later diverted for use in New Zealand. Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, shortfall penalties apply as follows: 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for an unacceptable tax position, and up to 150% for evasion or abusive tax positions; use-of-money interest accrues on any unpaid GST. False or misleading documentation can lead to prosecution. Records substantiating export zero-rating must be retained for at least seven years. The 180-day foreign exchange repatriation window is treated as a documentary benchmark; longer delays, non-repatriation, or unusual payment structures will trigger heightened audit scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised and convertible foreign exchange regime with no exchange control legislation or restrictions on the repatriation of capital, dividends, or loan repayments for foreign-owned entities. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) does not require prior approval for current account transactions such as trade settlements, service fees, or royalties, nor does it impose surrender requirements on export proceeds. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, intercompany loans, and equity injections, are similarly free from RBNZ exchange control approval, although certain transactions may trigger notification requirements under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 if they involve significant business assets or sensitive land. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely floating in the international markets, and authorised banks are permitted to facilitate spot and forward FX transactions without restriction. In practice, profitability remittance hurdles are minimal, limited to standard corporate governance documentation such as board resolutions, audited financial statements, tax residency certificates, and compliance with the New Zealand Inland Revenue Department's withholding tax obligations on dividends and interest. Because there is no currency inconvertibility risk, offshore treasury operations can maintain multi-currency accounts and execute hedging instruments directly with domestic and global banks. The AML/CFT framework, administered by the RBNZ alongside the Department of Internal Affairs and the Financial Markets Authority, focuses on customer due diligence, beneficial ownership transparency, and suspicious transaction reporting rather than on FX controls. Therefore, the primary frictions for a NZ corporate account are KYC-related, not FX regulatory barriers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory surrender requirements on export foreign currency receipts. Exporters may retain all proceeds in foreign currency accounts or convert them to NZD at their discretion. There is no mandatory timeline or conversion ratio under any New Zealand statute; the only obligations are standard tax reporting and AML/CFT record-keeping.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI entities such as Wise, Airwallex, and Revolut generally hold an NZ money service provider registration or operate through an NZ-registered entity; their viability for servicing a New Zealand limited company is Medium-to-High for transaction execution but Low relative to Tier-1 domestic banks for capital escrow and local regulatory compliance. Wise is integrated into the target payment rails and is viable for small-trade disbursements and FX conversion, but it is not a substitute for a New Zealand bank settlement account under corporate treasury standards. The RBNZ's AML/CFT supervisor treats EMIs as reporting entities, and overseas EMIs without an NZ financial service provider licence cannot legally onboard NZ corporates as a primary bank. Therefore, the recommended solution is a domestic Tier-1 bank account for statutory capital and operational settlements, supplemented by Wise for low-value fast payments, not for principal liquidity clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banks do not statutorily require directors to appear physically in-branch; remote onboarding via video call and digital identity verification is generally permitted. However, for a foreign-incorporated entity (or a NZ company with offshore directors), most Tier-1 banks mandate that at least one director or senior signatory complete a recorded virtual interview, present original or notarised passports, and provide certified copies of incorporation documents. In practice, banks may require a physical presence for the first account opening when the beneficial ownership structure is complex, but consular proxy opening is not formally recognised as a standard path; instead, a licensed legal counsel or chartered accountant in New Zealand can act as an introducer or authorised verifier under the bank's AML/CFT program.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction origin of funding or beneficial owner residency in a FATF-monitored jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of wealth declaration covering the past 24 months, bank statements from the originator institution, signed audited financial statements of the parent entity, tax residency certificates for all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), and an independent legal opinion confirming the funds' provenance and absence of sanctions exposure

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership chain through a Cyrpus or offshore trust structure where UBO percentage cannot be established at first pass
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trust deed, memorandum and articles of association, group organisational chart showing each shareholder and nominee, a register of directors and UBOs signed by the local director, a letter from the licensed trustee or trust administrator confirming settlor and beneficiary classes, and notarised passport copies of all individuals with 25% or greater control

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity mismatch between low-risk civil engineering BIM outsourcing and large upfront capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts or master service agreements with overseas clients, detailed business financial forecast and cash-flow model, payroll plan for New Zealand-based drafting engineers, corporate bank reference letters from existing banking partners, and statutory declaration of business purpose by the local director

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual payment rail preference for the target matrix, notably the use of Wise plus direct SWIFT for trade disbursements absent a clear treasury rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy document, annual trade volume estimates and counterparty list, evidence of commercial comparison between SWIFT and low-cost rails, and the company's AML/CFT compliance manual appointing an external consultant who will monitor cross-border transaction patterns

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for a New Zealand limited company is routed as share subscription proceeds or shareholder loans through SWIFT MT103 from the parent company's bank. The remittance should clearly state the purpose code 'C07' under the OECD standard or its New Zealand equivalent for capital investment, referencing the shareholder resolution and the share allotment certificate. New Zealand does not require formal FX control approval or capital verification, but the bank will require a copy of the board resolution authorising the issue of shares, a completed client tax information questionnaire (W-8BEN-E if US-related), and a declaration as to the source of funds. The funds must be received in NZD through a domestic Tier-1 bank settlement account to allow for proper value dating and downstream disbursements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for BIM/CAD services are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for client invoice settlements and vendor payments, with ICC Uniform Rules for Forfaiting applicable only if receivables are discounted. Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) are suitable for large physical project contracts, while Documentary Collections are used for low-risk drafting deliverables. For sub-$10,000 disbursements, Wise provides faster but the actual clearing is still via domestic New Zealand settlements; all outbound payments must include a correct payment purpose code and beneficiary KYC package. The company should maintain dedicated NZD and USD accounts to optimise currency conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward FX contracts with a registered New Zealand bank for up to 12 months without underlying trade documentation restrictions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only in restricted offshore markets; for NZD/USD, deliverable forwards are standard and NDFs are not normally required
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between NZD and USD for intercompany loan or capex hedging subject to ISDA master agreement execution
FX options for risk management purposes only, requiring board-approved treasury policy and prudent accounting treatment under NZ IFRS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Companies Act 1993 annual return confirming registered office, address for service, directors, members and shareholding structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the Registrar-assigned Annual Return Date (ARD), normally the incorporation anniversary or a balance-date-aligned date approved by the Registrar; the Companies Office issues a reminder approximately 21 days before the ARD
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offense under section 211 of the Companies Act 1993 with a maximum fine of NZ$100; continued non-filing exposes the company to removal (strike-off) notices under sections 318-320 of the Companies Act 1993 and eventual deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and statutory audit report filed with the Registrar (large company regime only)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Large companies only: filing required within 20 working days after the Annual Return Date; NZ_LTD remains below the large-company thresholds and is exempt from filing audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalties under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for non-filing, director prosecution exposure, and continued default may lead to Registrar removal action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders meeting and minute book recording (triggered regime under section 120 of the Companies Act 1993)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained in the company minute book at the registered office; no government filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Only when required by the constitution or a valid shareholder request; a convened annual meeting must be held within 6 months after the company balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who unreasonably refuse to convene a required annual meeting commit an offense under the Companies Act 1993 and may be subject to monetary penalties under the general offense provisions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is compulsory only for a large company meeting at least two of three tests in the current and preceding accounting periods: total assets above NZ$33 million, total revenue above NZ$10 million, or 50 or more full-time employees; an audit may also be triggered by the constitution or by shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights. NZ_LTD, as a low-asset engineering CAD and BIM services company, does not meet the compulsory audit thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with accounting standards issued by the New Zealand External Reporting Board (XRB): NZ IFRS for Tier 1 entities, NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime for Tier 2 entities, or the NZ Simple Format Reporting framework for Tier 3 and Tier 4 small entities; all frameworks are IFRS-consistent for corporate reporting purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members, and the Companies Office annual return operates as the annual statutory confirmation of members, directors, share structure and registered office details. A separate annual UBO confirmation filing is not yet in force for ordinary New Zealand private companies; the Companies (Disclosure of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2022 has not been commenced and remains subject to government review.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - 600 (registered office and basic company secretarial services; Companies Office annual return filing fee is nil)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 at statutory exempt status; voluntary independent audit for a small engineering CAD and BIM service entity typically ranges from USD 6,000 to USD 18,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays; R&D tax credit of 15% on eligible expenditure; loss carryforward indefinite subject to 49% shareholder continuity or business continuity test.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via myIR (Inland Revenue's online portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 7 months after the company's balance date (e.g., for a 31 March balance date, deadline is 7 November)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross income derived from New Zealand sources; foreign income may be exempt if not attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment.
Claim only expenses directly incurred in deriving New Zealand-sourced income; apportionment required for mixed-use expenses.
Ensure all transfer pricing adjustments are reflected; non-resident companies must file if they have a New Zealand permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., R&D credit, foreign tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits for which the company is eligible; attach supporting documentation.
Pay any balance due by the deadline; provisional tax payments made during the year are credited.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 for the first day, plus NZ$50 per day up to NZ$1,000; late payment penalty of 1% per month on unpaid tax; further penalties for inaccurate returns up to 150% of the tax shortfall.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced treaty rate (e.g., 15% under NZ-Australia DTA), the non-resident shareholder must provide a Certificate of Residence (CoR) from their home tax authority and complete an IRD form (IR3NR or equivalent) to the payer. The payer must retain the CoR and apply the reduced rate at source. If the full 30% is withheld, the shareholder may claim a refund from Inland Revenue by filing a non-resident tax return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 15% (treaty rates often 5% or 10% depending on jurisdiction); Interest: statutory 15% (treaty rates often 10% or 0% for certain financial institutions).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZ$1 million aggregate cross-border related party transactions (goods, services, intangibles, interest) triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) akin to offshore jurisdictions; however, general anti-avoidance rules (Part IVA of the Income Tax Act 2007) and treaty abuse provisions (Principal Purpose Test) apply. Companies must demonstrate real economic substance (e.g., office, employees, decision-making) to claim treaty benefits and avoid recharacterisation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating income, overstating deductions, or failing to file returns with intent to evade tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty up to 150% of the tax shortfall; criminal conviction may result in imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to NZ$50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly participate in evasion; civil restitution orders and travel bans may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a conduit without real business activity, employees, or physical presence, particularly to claim treaty benefits or shift profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may disregard the entity for tax purposes, deny treaty relief, and impose penalties up to 100% of the tax avoided; interest on unpaid tax accrues.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if the company is a sham; they may face disqualification as directors and asset freezing orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, report suspicious transactions, or maintain required records under the AML/CFT Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties up to NZ$2 million for companies; criminal penalties up to NZ$300,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers can be personally liable for AML breaches; they may face fines, imprisonment, and prohibition from managing companies.
